chapter: Tulsa bands, Trent, Holder and Kirk
title: Phil Dorsey, Ponca City, and arranger Dave Duncan
summary: Promoter Phil Dorsey steers work to the band; in Ponca City trombonist Dave Duncan offers arrangements, and a call comes from the east Texas oil boom.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: As I said, I was just tickled over Roy and we would play and were doing pretty good, and a young man came to town--did you ever know a Phil Dorsey?
Well, this Phil Dorsey was from Omaha originally, but I guess that is before you got into the business, and he was

hanging around--he came with some group--but he was a musician, but he was some kind of promoter and talked way down deep in his stomach--a very intelligent guy, and he goes, you've got a pretty good band, Fields, and said, I'm going back to Omaha and I don't (inaudible), and he said, I'm going to get you up in that area, but he had good connections around in Kansas. And so, sure enough, he did come and he gave me a call.

No, not Howard White, this Phil Dorsey (Inaudible). At the same time, before then we--they were doing doing this taxi dance, ten cents a dance, and we got to play a few of those and it caught on I go to Ponca (phonetic spelling) City.
So then a white trombone player came down, Dave Duncan, and he said I like your band, how come somebody else (inaudible). He

said he was down somewhere and wanted to join Jack Teagarden, but he had a small group and so he couldn't hire me and here you are, you're a trombone with a little group, so I guess you say you don't need me, and he said, let me tell you, I can do more than that. He said, I arrange and I can play piano. So I said, you're an arranger and he already was on me that he wanted to do something a little different, not just play, because I had already began to buy stocks--you know, arrangements, but I always like to have different, if we could.

So I said, we could try to see what we could figure out, and he says, okay now, and he gave me his address. I didn't take him right then and he laughed, he said you're just trying to be nice and I said no, I'm going to try and figure out something. I got back into Tulsa and I had a call from Gladewater, Texas, they wanted bands down there, there's this big oil boom in east Texas then and wanted a band in Texas. Now, Gladewater and Longview in not
far from Nacodoches, so I said to some of the boys, I'll have to go down and see where I was born, and we laughed.
Did you have any people left in Nacodoches?
